messages:
maria: Thinking about a safer way to enable full request/response logs for short-lived canaries and debug sessions. We need something that doesn't permanently widen PII exposure but lets SREs repro live issues.
raj: yes please. current approach of toggling route-level full-logs is scary in prod. what are you thinking re: access controls?
maria: proposal: ephemeral debug sessions that 1) create a timeboxed JWT-backed session id, 2) enable full plaintext capture for matching traffic only, 3) store blobs encrypted with a per-session KMS key, 4) auto-delete after TTL (default 2 hours). ops must request via console or CLI and approval is logged.
olivia: :thinking_face: need to evaluate PII risk. My take: allow full capture only if PII detectors (regex + ML detector) run before storage and tag any hits; require an owner attestation. Also we should pseudonymize user identifiers by hashing with a per-session salt.
kevin: technical notes: we can implement per-session KMS envelope keys using our existing KMS integration. Key metadata should include `debug_session_id` and `requested_by`. Decryption keys can be time-limited and require RBAC check.
david: how does routing/sampling interact? If we enable debug session on a route that's high QPS we can't capture everything. We should allow sampling rules: capture N requests matching route + filter, or capture first error per user for X minutes.
maria: exactly. proposed config (console + CLI):
```
debug_session {
  id: "uuid"
  route_selector: "/v1/generate/*"
  match_filter: "status >= 500 or contains(error_code)"
  sample_mode: "first_n_per_minute"
  sample_n: 10
  ttl_seconds: 7200
  approve_by: "team/infra"
  redact_level: "post-detect"  # options: mask, redact, pseudonymize
}
```
raj: we also need telemetry consumers to opt in. billing, evals, and oncall pipelines should never read PII unless flagged and audited. Suggest a metadata flag `contains_sensitive` that blocks downstream unless explicit approver list present.
olivia: For the detection step: run streaming detectors before writing. If confidence > 0.9, redact inline (replace with `<REDACTED_TYPE>`); if 0.6-0.9, mark and surface to approver UI. We should avoid false positives blocking debug.
kevin: performance: do detection in async pipeline but keep an encrypted raw buffer for X minutes until detection completes; if detection finds PII, we scrub and re-encrypt. That way we don't block request path. Must ensure buffer TTL <= session TTL.
david: console UX: Admins should see active sessions, who requested, sample rules, and a one-click revoke which rotates KMS envelope key and triggers deletion. Also expose an audit trail CSV export.
maria: access model: only SRE+oncall+owner can request; requests to cross-cust data routes require legal sign-off. Also propose using salted-hash for user ids: `sha256(session_salt + user_id)` so raw ids are never in logs.
raj: re retention: default 2 hours, max 7 days with explicit exec-level signoff and separate billing/approval workflow. Any extension must create a tied ticket that auto-expires.
olivia: we should document allowed fields in these debug blobs. For example `headers.authorization` must be masked, `body.email` redacted unless approver allows. Keep schema strict.
kevin: implementation plan: small middleware to gate capture, an async detector worker, per-session S3 path with SSE-KMS, and console + CLI flows. ETA for prototype: 3 weeks.
david: one more: include tamper-evident digest in audit log so we can prove deletion occurred.
maria: OK I'll draft a short RFC and an initial console mock. Asking: who can review the security/PII section? @olivia @raj pls ack if you can take a look.
olivia: I can review this week.
raj: I'll take infra/KMS and RBAC bits.
opsbot: audit: debug session created by maria at 1999994321, id=uuid-9a1b, approver=auto (owner).
maria: thanks everyone — I'll put an RFC in docs and ping infra/design for AM. :thumbsup:
